evidence.contextAndScope: Chapter31 covers TF-A BL31 runtime-service registration, SMCCC request dispatch boundaries, PSCI/SDEI/RAS roles, firmware memory placement and latency claims.
evidence.problemSignalAndCounterevidence: The earlier text presented one dispatch implementation, fixed OEN allocations, universal service membership, board memory maps, stack sizes and measured SMC latency as general facts. It also described unsupported HVC rejection, SDEI/RAS behavior, BL33 entry level and register handling. The read-only evaluation calls out inconsistent stack sizing and unsupported latency/clobber claims.
evidence.causeHypothesisAndAlternatives: TF-A framework documentation, one presumed source revision, board-specific setup and invented measurements had been combined without identifying a TF-A tag, platform port, ELF or target board. A release-scoped reference explanation is safer than claiming a universal implementation trace.
evidence.evidence: TF-A 2.15 EL3 Runtime Service Writer’s Guide documents DECLARE_RT_SVC fields, descriptor collection by the BL31 linker script, initialization/validation and runtime lookup. TF-A Firmware Design describes BL31 as runtime firmware and PSCI’s role. These primary docs do not establish a particular product’s service set, memory addresses or latency.

evidence.decision: Remediated as a framework-boundary guide. Corrected the title and description because the previous metadata promised a PSCI/SDEI/RAS dispatcher trace and latency analysis that the supported, reproducible scope could not substantiate.

evidence.contextAndScope: Chapter32 explains SMCCC call transport, PSCI power-management semantics, Linux firmware discovery and CPU_ON lifecycle.
evidence.problemSignalAndCounterevidence: The earlier text mixed SMC32/SMC64 identifiers, argument/result widths and fast/yielding classifications; contained contradictory function-ID examples; described board-specific power-state encodings and reset registers; and presented synthetic latency and boot logs as measurements. The read-only evaluation specifically flags the SMC32/SMC64 identifier mismatch and unverified ABI details.
evidence.causeHypothesisAndAlternatives: A PSCI revision, Linux source snapshot and multiple unrelated SoC examples were combined as if they described one implementation. The revised text separates the SMCCC transport contract from PSCI semantics and directs version-specific details to the relevant normative documents and kernel binding.
evidence.evidence: Arm DEN0022 specifies the PSCI interface; Arm DEN0028 specifies SMCCC. Linux’s PSCI device-tree binding documents the firmware node and compatible/method properties. The primary references do not validate an unspecified SoC’s reset controller or timing.

evidence.contextAndScope: Chapter33 compares PSCI and spin-table contracts for Linux AArch64 secondary CPU startup, including relevant device-tree requirements and verification boundaries.
evidence.problemSignalAndCounterevidence: The earlier text asserted a universal single-primary boot sequence and fixed kernel internals, included a cpu-release-addr value exceeding one DT cell, and supplied unsupported GIC/register flows and fabricated bring-up timings/logs. The read-only evaluation independently confirms the malformed one-cell release-address example and questions timing interpretation.
evidence.causeHypothesisAndAlternatives: Kernel internals from an unspecified version and a board-specific boot sequence had been described as the universal Arm64 path. A versioned boot protocol and generic firmware contracts provide a supported explanation without pretending to reproduce a kernel build.
evidence.evidence: Linux arm64 boot protocol specifies that spin-table release storage is a naturally aligned, zero-initialized 64-bit location in reserved memory, describes the primary write/secondary branch behavior, and states that PSCI systems use CPU_ON. Arm DEN0022 defines PSCI; Linux PSCI DT binding documents the firmware node.
evidence.sampleCoverage: Read the full article and published-loop-04 annotations, including single-CPU premise, spin-table addresses/code, PSCI DT, Linux startup pseudocode, secondary assembly/percpu/GIC descriptions, hotplug, timing/log output, pitfalls, series-ending claim, links, title and description. Replaced version-specific execution narrative and synthetic measurements with protocol-level comparison and explicit target verification steps. No QEMU, Linux kernel image, board or runtime trace was available.
evidence.decision: Remediated to distinguish documented startup contracts from kernel implementation details. Corrected the malformed address example into an explicit placeholder, removed invented measurements, and corrected title/description and next-chapter metadata text to match the actual article scope and series order.
